title: The diagram shows the melting points of some Group I elements.
context: What is the melting point of potassium?
explanation:
Potassium is between sodium and rubidium in Group I, so its melting point is between theirs. The value is about 63.5 °C.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Melting points decrease down Group I.
  2. Sodium melts at about 98 °C and rubidium at about 39 °C on the graph.
  3. Potassium lies between sodium and rubidium in the group, so its melting point is intermediate.
  4. The only suitable value is 63.5 °C.

Check each option

  • A. Too high; this is above lithium and even above sodium.
  • B. Still too high for potassium.
  • C. Correct: potassium melts at about 63.5 °C.
  • D. Too low; this is closer to caesium/rubidium values.

Exam key idea: For Group I, melting points decrease down the group.

title: Which row about the similarities and differences between chlorine and bromine is correct?
options: Both are gases at room temperature and pressure; Chlorine and bromine have different colours.
Both exist as diatomic molecules; Chlorine is denser than bromine.
Both have atoms with seven outer-shell electrons; Only bromine will react with aqueous sodium chloride.
Both react with aqueous potassium iodide; Chlorine is more reactive than bromine.
answer: D. Both react with aqueous potassium iodide; Chlorine is more reactive than bromine.
explanation:
Chlorine and bromine are both halogens. They both react with iodide ions, and chlorine is more reactive than bromine.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Halogens have seven outer-shell electrons.
  2. Bromine is a liquid at room temperature, so row A is wrong.
  3. Chlorine and bromine both exist as diatomic molecules, but bromine is denser than chlorine, so row B is wrong.
  4. Both react with aqueous potassium iodide, and chlorine is above bromine in Group VII so it is more reactive.

Check each option

  • A. Incorrect because bromine is not a gas at room temperature.
  • B. Incorrect because chlorine is not denser than bromine.
  • C. Incorrect because bromine does not react with sodium chloride solution in that way.
  • D. Correct: both react with KI(aq), and chlorine is more reactive than bromine.

Exam key idea: For halogens: same outer-shell pattern, reactivity decreases down the group.

title: Which property of a metal is necessary for the named use?
explanation:
Food containers need a metal that resists corrosion. Otherwise the metal would react with food or the environment.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Ductile means drawn into wires; car bodies need malleability rather than ductility.
  2. Cutlery does conduct heat, but that is not the key property for its use.
  3. Food containers must resist corrosion so they do not react easily.
  4. Overhead cables should have low density, not high density.

Check each option

  • A. Incorrect: ductility is mainly needed for wires.
  • B. Incorrect: heat conduction is not the essential matching property here.
  • C. Correct: corrosion resistance is necessary for food containers.
  • D. Incorrect: high density is not an advantage for overhead cables.

Exam key idea: Match the use to the essential property, not just any true property of metals.

title: The equation for the reaction between magnesium and aqueous copper(II) sulfate is shown.
context:
Mg + CuSO4 → Cu + MgSO4

Which statement is correct?
options: Copper ions are oxidised to copper metal during the reaction.
Copper is displaced because it is more reactive than magnesium.
The oxidation number of magnesium decreases during the reaction.
The reaction happens because magnesium has a greater tendency to form positive ions than copper.
answer: D. The reaction happens because magnesium has a greater tendency to form positive ions than copper.
explanation:
Magnesium is more reactive than copper. It loses electrons more readily and forms Mg2+ ions, displacing copper from solution.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Mg changes from 0 in Mg(s) to +2 in MgSO₄, so magnesium is oxidised.
  2. Cu²⁺ changes to Cu(s), so copper ions are reduced, not oxidised.
  3. A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its compound.
  4. Therefore magnesium reacts because it has a greater tendency to form positive ions than copper.

Check each option

  • A. Incorrect: Cu²⁺ is reduced to Cu.
  • B. Incorrect: magnesium, not copper, is more reactive.
  • C. Incorrect: magnesium oxidation number increases from 0 to +2.
  • D. Correct: magnesium more readily forms positive ions.

Exam key idea: In displacement reactions, the more reactive metal is oxidised and forms ions.

title: Steel is an alloy of iron.
context:
Zinc is used to protect a steel car body from rusting. The steel body is completely coated in zinc.

Which statements about this use of zinc are correct?

  1. The layer of zinc prevents oxygen reaching the steel to cause rust.
  2. Zinc is used because it is a more reactive metal than iron.
  3. If the zinc layer is scratched, the steel will rust.
explanation:
Zinc protects steel both as a barrier and as a sacrificial metal. So statements 1 and 2 are correct, but statement 3 is not.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. The zinc coating acts as a barrier, stopping oxygen and water reaching the steel.
  2. Zinc is more reactive than iron, so it corrodes preferentially and protects the iron.
  3. If the coating is scratched, nearby zinc still offers sacrificial protection.
  4. So statements 1 and 2 are correct, but 3 is false.

Check each option

  • A. Incorrect because statement 3 is false.
  • B. Correct: statements 1 and 2 only.
  • C. Incorrect because statement 2 is also true.
  • D. Incorrect because statement 1 is true and statement 3 is false.

Exam key idea: Galvanising protects by barrier action and sacrificial protection.

title: Which test results show that a sample of water is pure?
context:
1. Its boiling point is 100 °C.
  2. Its freezing point is 0 °C.
  3. It turns anhydrous cobalt(II) chloride from blue to pink.
  4. It turns anhydrous copper(II) sulfate from white to blue.
explanation:
Pure substances have fixed melting/freezing and boiling points. The cobalt chloride and copper sulfate tests only show that water is present.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Pure water boils at 100 °C and freezes at 0 °C at standard pressure.
  2. The colour changes of cobalt chloride and copper sulfate are just tests for water.
  3. They do not prove the water is pure because impure water would also give those changes.
  4. So only statements 1 and 2 show purity.

Check each option

  • A. Correct: boiling point and freezing point indicate purity.
  • B. Incorrect: statement 4 only shows water is present.
  • C. Incorrect: statement 3 only shows water is present.
  • D. Incorrect: both 3 and 4 are tests for water, not purity.

Exam key idea: Tests for water are different from tests for pure water.

title: Which mixture of salts can be used as an NPK fertiliser?
explanation:
An NPK fertiliser must provide nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium. Only ammonium phosphate plus potassium sulfate supplies all three.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Ammonium phosphate contains nitrogen and phosphorus.
  2. Potassium sulfate supplies potassium.
  3. The other mixtures are missing at least one of N, P or K.
  4. Therefore option A is correct.

Check each option

  • A. Correct: this mixture supplies N, P and K.
  • B. Incorrect: no potassium compound is present.
  • C. Incorrect: no phosphorus compound is present.
  • D. Incorrect: sodium phosphate contains P but not K, and ammonium nitrate adds N only.

Exam key idea: Check each salt for the nutrient ions N, P and K.

title: Three air pollutants, X, Y and Z, are described.
context:
X is a toxic gas formed by the incomplete combustion of fossil fuels.

Y is formed by decomposing vegetation and increases global warming.

Z is a cause of breathing problems and acid rain.

What are X, Y and Z?
answer: A. carbon monoxide; methane; nitrogen oxides
explanation:
X is carbon monoxide, Y is methane and Z is nitrogen oxides.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Carbon monoxide is the toxic gas produced by incomplete combustion.
  2. Methane is released when vegetation decomposes anaerobically and is a greenhouse gas.
  3. Nitrogen oxides cause acid rain and breathing problems.
  4. Therefore row A matches all three descriptions.

Check each option

  • A. Correct: CO, methane and nitrogen oxides fit the descriptions.
  • B. Incorrect: particulates do not fit Y, and carbon dioxide does not fit Z.
  • C. Incorrect: sulfur dioxide is not formed by incomplete combustion in this way.
  • D. Incorrect: these pollutants do not match the three descriptions.

Exam key idea: Learn common pollutant sources and effects.

title: Which statement about members of the carboxylic acid homologous series is correct?
options: They have the same empirical formula and similar chemical properties.
They have the same empirical formula and their displayed formula differs by a –CH<sub>2</sub>– unit.
They have the same functional group and the same physical properties.
They have the same functional group and similar chemical properties.
answer: D. They have the same functional group and similar chemical properties.
explanation:
Members of a homologous series have the same functional group and similar chemical properties.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. A homologous series has a common functional group.
  2. Successive members differ by a –CH₂– unit.
  3. They have similar chemical properties, but physical properties show a gradual trend rather than staying the same.
  4. They do not all have the same empirical formula.

Check each option

  • A. Incorrect: empirical formula is not the defining feature.
  • B. Incorrect: displayed formula differs by –CH₂–, but empirical formula is not the same throughout.
  • C. Incorrect: physical properties are not the same.
  • D. Correct: same functional group and similar chemical properties.

Exam key idea: Homologous series: same functional group, similar chemistry, gradual physical-property changes.

title: Which of the named compounds have the correct structural formula?
context:
1. ethanoic acid, CH3CH2COOH
  2. propan-2-ol, CH3CH(OH)CH3
  3. but-2-ene, CH3CH=CHCH3
explanation:
Propan-2-ol and but-2-ene are correctly matched, but CH3CH2COOH is propanoic acid, not ethanoic acid.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Ethanoic acid is CH₃COOH, so statement 1 is false.
  2. CH₃CH(OH)CH₃ is propan-2-ol, so statement 2 is true.
  3. CH₃CH=CHCH₃ is but-2-ene, so statement 3 is true.
  4. Therefore the correct pair is 2 and 3.

Check each option

  • A. Incorrect because statement 1 is false.
  • B. Incorrect because statement 1 is false.
  • C. Correct: 2 and 3 only.
  • D. Incorrect because statement 2 is also true.

Exam key idea: Check both the carbon chain length and the position of the functional group or double bond.

title: The diagram shows a simple fractionating column for petroleum.
context: Which outlet produces the fraction with the most viscous liquids?
explanation:
The most viscous liquids are found near the bottom of the fractionating column.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Fractions with higher boiling points condense lower down the column.
  2. These larger molecules are more viscous.
  3. Outlet D is the lowest labelled side outlet.
  4. So D gives the most viscous liquids.

Check each option

  • A. Incorrect: top fractions are the least viscous.
  • B. Incorrect: still too high in the column.
  • C. Incorrect: more viscous fractions are lower.
  • D. Correct: the lowest outlet gives the most viscous liquids.

Exam key idea: In a fractionating column, larger molecules condense lower down.

title: Propene reacts separately with:
context:
• liquid bromine, Br2
  • hydrogen gas, H2
  • steam, H2O

Which statement about these three reactions is correct?
options: Two of the reactions are addition reactions and one is a substitution reaction.
The products of all three of these reactions are molecules containing exactly 9 atoms.
The products of two of these reactions are molecules containing exactly 9 atoms.
The products of two of these reactions are molecules containing exactly 11 atoms.
answer: D. The products of two of these reactions are molecules containing exactly 11 atoms.
explanation:
All three are addition reactions, and two of the products contain 11 atoms.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Propene adds bromine to form C₃H₆Br₂, which has 11 atoms total.
  2. Propene adds hydrogen to form propane, C₃H₈, which also has 11 atoms.
  3. Propene adds steam to form propanol, C₃H₈O, which has 12 atoms.
  4. Therefore two of the products contain exactly 11 atoms.

Check each option

  • A. Incorrect: all three are addition reactions.
  • B. Incorrect: the three products do not all have 9 atoms.
  • C. Incorrect: none of the three matching products give exactly two with 9 atoms.
  • D. Correct: bromination and hydrogenation each give products with 11 atoms.

Exam key idea: For alkenes, reactions with bromine, hydrogen and steam are all addition reactions.

title: Polymers are described as addition polymers or condensation polymers.
context: Which two rows give a correct statement about each type of polymerisation?
explanation:
Rows 2 and 3 are correct. Addition polymerisation uses monomers with double bonds and produces no other products; condensation polymerisation uses monomers with suitable functional groups and forms a small molecule as well.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Row 1 is wrong for both sides.
  2. Row 2 is correct: addition gives no other product, condensation produces a small molecule.
  3. Row 3 is correct: addition monomers have a double bond and condensation monomers have different functional groups.
  4. Row 4 is wrong because nylon is a condensation polymer, not an addition polymer.

Check each option

  • A. Incorrect because row 1 is wrong.
  • B. Incorrect because row 1 is wrong.
  • C. Correct: rows 2 and 3.
  • D. Incorrect because row 4 is not fully correct.

Exam key idea: Know the monomers and products for each polymerisation type.
tableRows: A small molecule is produced as a second product.

title: Alanine is an amino acid. The structural formula of alanine is shown.
context:
It is the only monomer in a polymer.

Which diagram represents a section of this polymer?
explanation:
Amino acids form polyamides (proteins) with repeating peptide links, –NH–CH(R)–CO–. For alanine, R = CH₃.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. When amino acids polymerise, the –COOH group of one reacts with the –NH₂ group of another to form a peptide link, –CONH–.
  2. For alanine, each repeating unit contains –NH–CH(CH₃)–CO–.
  3. Option C shows the correct repeating arrangement of atoms and peptide links.
  4. The other diagrams place the groups in the wrong order or include incorrect link types.

Check each option

  • A. Incorrect: the peptide-link arrangement is wrong.
  • B. Incorrect: the carbonyl and nitrogen sequence is not the correct alanine polymer repeat.
  • C. Correct: it shows repeated –NH–CH(CH₃)–CO– units.
  • D. Incorrect: it includes ester-type –COO– links rather than peptide links.

Exam key idea: For amino-acid polymers, look for the peptide link –CONH– in the repeating chain.

title: Which statements describe an environmental challenge caused by the disposal of plastics?
context:
1. The burning of the plastics can release toxic gases.
  2. Plastics are harmful to marine life.
  3. Plastics decompose very slowly in the environment.
explanation:
All three statements are correct.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Burning some plastics can release toxic gases.
  2. Plastic waste harms marine life through ingestion and entanglement.
  3. Most common plastics decompose very slowly, so they persist in the environment.
  4. So all three statements describe environmental challenges.

Check each option

  • A. Correct: 1, 2 and 3 are all true.
  • B. Incorrect: statement 3 is also true.
  • C. Incorrect: statement 2 is also true.
  • D. Incorrect: statement 1 is also true.

Exam key idea: Plastic-disposal problems include pollution, harm to wildlife and toxic emissions.

title: Magnesium reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to produce hydrogen gas.
context: Which pieces of apparatus are needed to determine the rate of this reaction?
explanation:
To determine rate here, you need to measure the gas volume and the time taken.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. The gas syringe (1) measures the volume of hydrogen produced.
  2. The stopwatch (2) measures time.
  3. A burette (3) and tripod (4) are not required to measure this rate directly.
  4. Therefore the needed apparatus are 1 and 2.

Check each option

  • A. Correct: gas syringe plus stopwatch.
  • B. Incorrect: a burette is not needed here.
  • C. Incorrect: a tripod does not measure rate.
  • D. Incorrect: neither of these gives the necessary pair of measurements.

Exam key idea: Rate needs a change measurement and a time measurement.

title: Solution X contains aqueous sulfite ions.
context: Which method describes the test for the aqueous sulfite ions in X?
options: Add nitric acid to X. The gas produced turns limewater cloudy.
Add nitric acid to X. The gas produced decolourises aqueous potassium manganate(VII).
Add nitric acid to X then add aqueous barium chloride to give a white precipitate.
Add nitric acid to X then add aqueous silver nitrate to give a pale yellow precipitate.
answer: B. Add nitric acid to X. The gas produced decolourises aqueous potassium manganate(VII).
explanation:
Acidified sulfites release sulfur dioxide, which decolourises aqueous potassium manganate(VII).

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Sulfite ions react with acid to form sulfur dioxide gas.
  2. Sulfur dioxide is a reducing agent that decolourises purple potassium manganate(VII) solution.
  3. Limewater cloudy is a test for carbon dioxide, not sulfur dioxide.
  4. Barium chloride after acidification is used for sulfate ions; silver nitrate is used for halides.

Check each option

  • A. Incorrect: turning limewater cloudy indicates carbon dioxide.
  • B. Correct: SO₂ decolourises aqueous potassium manganate(VII).
  • C. Incorrect: this is associated with sulfate testing, not sulfite.
  • D. Incorrect: pale yellow with silver nitrate indicates iodide.

Exam key idea: Sulfite + acid → sulfur dioxide, which is a reducing gas.

title: A chemical mixture is separated using paper chromatography.
context:
The chromatogram is shown.

Which statements are correct?

  1. The spot nearest the solvent front has an Rf value greater than 0.50.
  2. Insoluble compounds rise with the solvent front.
  3. The lower spot is a less soluble substance than the higher spot.
explanation:
Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The upper spot has moved more than half way to the solvent front, and the lower spot is less soluble.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Rf = distance moved by spot ÷ distance moved by solvent front. The upper spot has travelled more than half of the solvent-front distance.
  2. Substances must be soluble in the solvent to move up the paper, so statement 2 is false.
  3. A lower spot has moved less distance and is therefore less soluble in the solvent than the higher spot.
  4. So statements 1 and 3 are correct.

Check each option

  • A. Incorrect because statement 2 is false.
  • B. Incorrect because statement 2 is false.
  • C. Correct: 1 and 3 only.
  • D. Incorrect because statement 1 is also true.

Exam key idea: In chromatography, more soluble components travel further and have larger Rf values.

title: The arrangements of particles in solids, liquids and gases are different.
context: Which statement about the molecules in ice, water or steam is correct?
options: The H<sub>2</sub>O molecules are on average closest together in steam.
The H<sub>2</sub>O molecules are on average furthest apart in water.
The H<sub>2</sub>O molecules in steam have the second highest average velocity.
The H<sub>2</sub>O molecules in ice are able to vibrate.
answer: D. The H<sub>2</sub>O molecules in ice are able to vibrate.
explanation:
Molecules in a solid vibrate about fixed positions. Ice particles are not motionless.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Ice is a solid; its water molecules vibrate about fixed positions.
  2. Water molecules in steam are much further apart than in ice or liquid water.
  3. Steam molecules have the highest average speed of the three states under comparable heating conditions.
  4. Only option D accurately describes particle motion in ice.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Incorrect: steam particles are widely separated.
  • B. Incorrect: steam has the largest average separation.
  • C. Incorrect: steam has the highest, not second highest, average speed.
  • D. Correct: the molecules in ice can vibrate.

Exam key idea: Solids: vibrate; liquids: move past each other; gases: move freely.

chapter: States of Matter · Temperature and pressure
title: A sealed glass container contains 200 cm<sup>3</sup> of oxygen at 100 °C.
context:
The container is cooled to 25 °C.

Which row shows how the average kinetic energy of the oxygen molecules and the pressure inside the container change?
explanation:
Cooling a gas in a rigid sealed container decreases average kinetic energy and pressure.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Temperature falls from 100 °C to 25 °C, so the particles have lower average kinetic energy.
  2. Oxygen molecules travel more slowly and collide with the walls less forcefully and less frequently.
  3. The gas volume remains fixed by the sealed glass container.
  4. Pressure therefore decreases together with kinetic energy.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Correct: both quantities decrease.
  • B. Incorrect: pressure does not rise when the temperature falls at fixed volume.
  • C. Incorrect: average kinetic energy falls rather than rises.
  • D. Incorrect: both changes are in the wrong direction.

Exam key idea: For a fixed amount of gas at constant volume, pressure increases with absolute temperature.

chapter: Atoms and Compounds · Mixtures of compounds
title: ○ and ● represent atoms of different elements.
context: Which diagram represents a mixture of compounds?
explanation:
A mixture of compounds contains different types of molecules, each made from more than one element.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Diagram A shows only one element in diatomic molecules.
  2. Diagram B shows one type of compound repeated, a pure compound.
  3. Diagram C shows different molecular structures involving both elements: a mixture of compounds.
  4. Diagram D contains separate elemental molecules rather than compounds.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Incorrect: all particles contain only one element.
  • B. Incorrect: the particles are identical molecules of a single compound.
  • C. Correct: two kinds of compounds are present.
  • D. Incorrect: this is a mixture of elements, not compounds.

Exam key idea: A compound contains chemically joined atoms of different elements; a mixture has multiple substances.

title: Which statement explains why water is a compound?
options: Hydrogen and oxygen in water can only be separated using a chemical change.
Hydrogen and oxygen in water can be separated using a physical change.
The masses of hydrogen and oxygen combined in water are variable.
Water has the same properties as both hydrogen and oxygen.
answer: A. Hydrogen and oxygen in water can only be separated using a chemical change.
explanation:
Hydrogen and oxygen are chemically bonded in water and can only be separated by a chemical process.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. A compound consists of chemically bonded elements.
  2. Changing water into hydrogen and oxygen requires a chemical reaction such as electrolysis.
  3. Water has a fixed H:O atomic ratio of 2:1, not variable composition.
  4. Water has properties different from the elements it contains.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Correct: decomposition of the compound is a chemical change.
  • B. Incorrect: ordinary physical separation cannot split bonded H₂O.
  • C. Incorrect: a pure compound has fixed composition.
  • D. Incorrect: compounds usually have different properties from their elements.

Exam key idea: Elements within a compound must be chemically separated.

title: The table shows the number of protons, neutrons and electrons in four different particles.
context: Which two particles have the same chemical properties?
explanation:
W and Y are neutral atoms of the same element, chlorine, with different neutron numbers. They are isotopes and have the same chemical properties.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. W has 17 protons and 17 electrons; Y also has 17 protons and 17 electrons.
  2. These particles are both neutral chlorine atoms, with different neutrons (18 and 20).
  3. The number of electrons and their arrangement determine chemical properties.
  4. Therefore W and Y have the same chemical properties.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Incorrect: W and X have different proton and electron numbers.
  • B. Correct: W and Y are isotopes of chlorine.
  • C. Incorrect: X and Z are different elements/particles.
  • D. Incorrect: Y and Z have different proton numbers.

Exam key idea: Isotopes: same proton number, different neutron number, same electron configuration for neutral atoms.

title: Which statement explains why sodium chloride, NaCl, has a high melting point?
answer: A. NaCl contains strong ionic bonds.
explanation:
Sodium chloride has a giant ionic lattice with strong electrostatic attractions between oppositely charged ions.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. NaCl is composed of Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions arranged in a giant ionic lattice.
  2. Oppositely charged ions are held together by strong ionic bonds.
  3. A large amount of thermal energy is required to overcome these electrostatic attractions.
  4. Therefore NaCl has a high melting point.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Correct: strong ionic bonds require much energy to overcome.
  • B. Incorrect: NaCl is not a covalent structure.
  • C. Incorrect: ionic lattices are held by ionic bonds, not intermolecular forces between molecules.
  • D. Incorrect: metallic bonding occurs in metals, not sodium chloride.

Exam key idea: Ionic compounds often have high melting points because ionic attractions are strong.

title: Different forms of an element G are used as lubricants and in cutting tools.
context: What is the structure of G?
explanation:
Graphite and diamond are allotropes of carbon, both giant covalent structures.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Graphite contains layers of covalently bonded carbon atoms that slide over one another, making it a lubricant.
  2. Diamond has a strong three-dimensional covalent network, making it hard enough for cutting tools.
  3. Both are forms of carbon and both are giant covalent structures.
  4. The correct answer is A.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Correct: graphite and diamond are both giant covalent forms of carbon.
  • B. Incorrect: they do not consist of positive and negative ions.
  • C. Incorrect: carbon allotropes are not metallic lattices.
  • D. Incorrect: graphite and diamond do not form small separate molecules.

Exam key idea: Diamond: hard cutting; graphite: lubricating. Both are giant covalent.

title: Which row shows the correct formulas of iron(II) bromide and zinc nitrate?
explanation:
Iron(II) bromide is FeBr₂ and zinc nitrate is Zn(NO₃)₂.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Iron(II) means Fe²⁺; bromide is Br⁻, so two bromide ions balance one iron(II) ion.
  2. Zinc forms Zn²⁺ ions and nitrate is NO₃⁻.
  3. Two nitrate ions are needed to balance Zn²⁺; brackets group the polyatomic ion.
  4. Therefore the correct row is B.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Incorrect: zinc nitrate is missing a second nitrate ion.
  • B. Correct: both formulae have balanced ionic charges.
  • C. Incorrect: both formulae are wrong.
  • D. Incorrect: Fe₂Br is not charge balanced.

Exam key idea: Total positive charge must equal total negative charge.

title: Which statement defines relative molecular mass?
options: the sum of the relative atomic masses
the simplest whole number ratio of the different atoms in a molecule
the number and type of different atoms in a molecule
the average mass of the isotopes of an element compared to 1/12th of the mass of an atom of <sup>12</sup>C
answer: A. the sum of the relative atomic masses
explanation:
Relative molecular mass (Mr) is the sum of the relative atomic masses of all the atoms in a molecule.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Take the chemical formula of the molecule.
  2. Count how many atoms there are of each element.
  3. Multiply each count by the relevant relative atomic mass, then add the results.
  4. For H₂O, Mᵣ = 2×1 + 16 = 18.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Correct: it describes relative molecular mass.
  • B. Incorrect: this describes the empirical formula.
  • C. Incorrect: this describes molecular formula composition.
  • D. Incorrect: this describes relative atomic mass, not relative molecular mass.

Exam key idea: To calculate Mᵣ, sum all Aᵣ values in the molecule.

chapter: Stoichiometry · Limiting reactants and gas volume
title: The equation for the reaction between magnesium and dilute hydrochloric acid is shown.
context:
Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl2(aq) + H2(g)

0.10 mol Mg is added to 100 cm3 of 1.0 mol / dm3 HCl(aq).

The hydrogen produced is collected and its volume measured at room temperature and pressure.

What is the maximum volume of hydrogen produced?
explanation:
The maximum hydrogen volume is 1.2 dm³ at r.t.p. Hydrochloric acid is the limiting reactant.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Convert 100 cm³ to 0.100 dm³.
  2. Moles of HCl = concentration × volume = 1.0 × 0.100 = 0.100 mol.
  3. The equation requires 2 mol HCl to make 1 mol H₂, giving 0.050 mol H₂.
  4. Volume at r.t.p. = 0.050 × 24 dm³ = 1.2 dm³.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Incorrect: 0.05 is the amount in moles, not gas volume.
  • B. Correct: 0.05 mol × 24 dm³/mol = 1.2 dm³.
  • C. Incorrect: this assumes 0.1 mol H₂ and ignores the 2:1 HCl:H₂ ratio.
  • D. Incorrect: this doubles the amount and volume.

Exam key idea: Identify limiting reactant before calculating gas volume at r.t.p. (24 dm³/mol).

title: The apparatus shown is used to electroplate a copper spoon with silver.
context: Which row is correct?
options: silver; copper spoon; aqueous silver nitrate
silver; copper spoon; aqueous copper(II) chloride
copper spoon; silver; aqueous silver nitrate
copper spoon; silver; aqueous copper(II) nitrate
answer: A. silver; copper spoon; aqueous silver nitrate
explanation:
The spoon is the cathode, silver is the anode, and aqueous silver nitrate supplies Ag⁺ ions.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. The copper spoon is the object to be coated, so it is connected to the negative cathode.
  2. Silver ions gain electrons at the cathode and deposit as silver metal on the spoon.
  3. A silver anode dissolves to replace silver ions in the solution.
  4. An aqueous silver salt, such as silver nitrate, provides Ag⁺ ions; therefore option A is correct.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Correct: silver anode, copper-spoon cathode, AgNO₃(aq) electrolyte.
  • B. Incorrect: CuCl₂ does not supply Ag⁺ for silver plating.
  • C. Incorrect: the spoon must be the cathode, not the anode.
  • D. Incorrect: electrode roles and electrolyte are wrong.

Exam key idea: For electroplating, the object being plated is the cathode (−).

chapter: Electrochemistry · Electrolysis of dilute sulfuric acid
title: Dilute sulfuric acid is electrolysed using inert electrodes.
context: What is produced at the anode?
explanation:
Oxygen is produced at the anode. In dilute sulfuric acid with inert electrodes, water is discharged to make oxygen at the positive electrode.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. In electrolysis, the anode is the positive electrode where oxidation occurs.
  2. In dilute sulfuric acid, sulfate ions are not discharged under these conditions; water / hydroxide is oxidised instead.
  3. This produces oxygen gas at the anode.
  4. Hydrogen is produced at the cathode, not the anode.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Incorrect: hydrogen is formed at the cathode.
  • B. Correct: oxygen is released at the anode.
  • C. Incorrect: sulfur is not formed.
  • D. Incorrect: sulfur dioxide is not the anode product in this electrolysis.

Exam key idea: For dilute sulfuric acid with inert electrodes: cathode → hydrogen, anode → oxygen.

chapter: Electrochemistry · Copper(II) sulfate with copper electrodes
title: Aqueous copper(II) sulfate is a blue solution. The solution is electrolysed using copper electrodes.
context: Which row describes the changes that take place during the electrolysis?
answer: D. increases; decreases; stays the same
explanation:
The cathode gains mass, the anode loses mass, and the blue colour stays the same.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. At the cathode, Cu²⁺ ions gain electrons and plate out as copper metal, so the cathode mass increases.
  2. At the anode, copper atoms lose electrons and enter solution as Cu²⁺ ions, so the anode mass decreases.
  3. Because Cu²⁺ ions removed at the cathode are replaced by Cu²⁺ from the anode, the solution concentration stays nearly constant.
  4. Therefore the blue colour remains the same and row D is correct.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Incorrect: the cathode should gain mass, not lose it, and the solution colour stays the same.
  • B. Incorrect: the cathode does not decrease in mass.
  • C. Incorrect: the colour does not become paler because Cu²⁺ ions are replenished.
  • D. Correct: cathode increases, anode decreases, colour stays the same.

Exam key idea: With copper electrodes in CuSO₄(aq), copper simply transfers from anode to cathode.

title: Nitrogen trifluoride, NF₃, is used in the manufacture of certain types of solar panels. The equation for the formation of nitrogen trifluoride is shown.
context:
N2 + 3F2 → 2NF3

Using the table of bond energies, what is the energy change for this reaction?
explanation:
The reaction energy change is −280 kJ/mol. Use ΔH = bonds broken − bonds formed.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Break one N≡N bond: 950 kJ/mol.
  2. Break three F–F bonds: 3 × 150 = 450 kJ/mol. Total energy in = 1400 kJ/mol.
  3. Form six N–F bonds in 2NF₃: 6 × 280 = 1680 kJ/mol.
  4. ΔH = 1400 − 1680 = −280 kJ/mol, so option B is correct.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Incorrect: this value is too negative.
  • B. Correct: broken 1400 minus formed 1680 equals −280.
  • C. Incorrect: sign is wrong; the reaction is exothermic.
  • D. Incorrect: this is close to the total bond energies involved, not the net change.

Exam key idea: Bond energy calculation: ΔH = Σ(bonds broken) − Σ(bonds formed).

title: Ethanol and ethanoic acid react to form ethyl ethanoate and water.
context:
CH3CH2OH + CH3CO2H ⇌ CH3CO2CH2CH3 + H2O

Which statement explains why concentrated sulfuric acid is added to the reaction mixture?
options: The position of equilibrium moves to the left-hand side.
Sulfuric acid is a weaker acid than ethanoic acid.
The total frequency of collisions decreases.
Sulfuric acid acts as a catalyst for the reaction.
answer: D. Sulfuric acid acts as a catalyst for the reaction.
explanation:
Concentrated sulfuric acid acts as a catalyst for esterification. It can also help remove water, but among these options the correct reason is catalysis.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Esterification is slow at room conditions, so an acid catalyst is used.
  2. Concentrated sulfuric acid provides an acidic medium and speeds up the reaction pathway.
  3. A catalyst increases the rate without being used up.
  4. Therefore option D is the correct statement.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Incorrect: if water is removed, equilibrium tends to move right, not left.
  • B. Incorrect: sulfuric acid is stronger, not weaker, than ethanoic acid.
  • C. Incorrect: a catalyst does not reduce collision frequency.
  • D. Correct: sulfuric acid acts as a catalyst.

Exam key idea: In esterification, concentrated sulfuric acid is commonly used as the acid catalyst.

chapter: Rates of Reaction · Effect of concentration
title: Which statement explains why increasing the concentration of a reactant increases the rate of reaction?
options: There is a higher percentage of successful collisions between particles.
The activation energy of the reaction decreases.
There is a higher percentage of collisions involving particles with energy greater than the activation energy.
There are more collisions per second between particles.
answer: D. There are more collisions per second between particles.
explanation:
Increasing concentration increases the number of collisions per second.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Higher concentration means more reacting particles in the same volume.
  2. Particles are closer together and collide more often.
  3. The activation energy is unchanged, and the fraction with energy above Eₐ is mainly affected by temperature, not concentration.
  4. So the rate rises because there are more collisions per second.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Incorrect: concentration mainly changes collision frequency, not the percentage that succeed.
  • B. Incorrect: activation energy only changes with a catalyst.
  • C. Incorrect: this percentage is not increased by concentration alone.
  • D. Correct: more frequent collisions increase reaction rate.

Exam key idea: Concentration affects collision frequency; temperature affects the fraction above activation energy.

title: The Haber process is used to make ammonia.
context:
N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3

Which statements about the Haber process are correct?
explanation:
Statements 2 and 3 only are correct.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Nitrogen is obtained from the air, so statement 2 is true.
  2. Industrial hydrogen is obtained mainly from methane / natural gas, so statement 3 is true.
  3. Statement 1 is not the usual industrial source of hydrogen.
  4. Statement 4 is false because the pressure is high (about 200 atm), not 1 atm, although iron is the catalyst.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Incorrect: statement 1 is false.
  • B. Incorrect: statement 4 is false because the pressure is wrong.
  • C. Incorrect: statement 4 is still false, so this option is not fully correct.
  • D. Correct: only statements 2 and 3 are correct.

Exam key idea: Haber process: N₂ from air, H₂ from methane, iron catalyst, high pressure.

title: The equation represents the reaction between sulfur dioxide and acidified potassium dichromate(VI).
context:
3SO2 + Cr2O72− + 2H+ → 3SO42− + 2Cr3+ + H2O

What is oxidised and what is the oxidising agent in this reaction?
explanation:
SO₂ is oxidised, and dichromate(VI) ions are the oxidising agent.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Sulfur in SO₂ increases in oxidation state as it becomes sulfate, so SO₂ is oxidised.
  2. Dichromate(VI), Cr₂O₇²⁻, is reduced to Cr³⁺.
  3. A species that is reduced causes oxidation of the other species, so it is the oxidising agent.
  4. Therefore the correct pair is SO₂ and Cr₂O₇²⁻.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Incorrect: dichromate is reduced, not oxidised, and H⁺ is not the oxidising agent.
  • B. Incorrect: dichromate is the oxidising agent but it is not oxidised.
  • C. Correct: SO₂ is oxidised and Cr₂O₇²⁻ is the oxidising agent.
  • D. Incorrect: H⁺ is not the oxidising agent here.

Exam key idea: Oxidising agent = species that gets reduced while oxidising the other substance.

chapter: Rates of Reaction · Strong and weak acids
title: A known mass of magnesium is added to excess dilute hydrochloric acid.
context:
The total volume of hydrogen produced is 70 cm3.

The experiment is repeated using dilute ethanoic acid in place of dilute hydrochloric acid.

All other conditions are the same.

Which row gives the relative rate of the reaction and the total volume of hydrogen produced in the second experiment?
explanation:
The reaction is slower, but the total volume of hydrogen stays 70 cm³.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Hydrochloric acid is a strong acid, while ethanoic acid is a weak acid.
  2. A weak acid provides a lower concentration of H⁺ ions, so the reaction with magnesium is slower.
  3. The same mass of magnesium is used, and the acid is still in excess, so the same total moles of hydrogen are produced.
  4. Therefore the total gas volume remains 70 cm³, but the rate is slower.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Incorrect: the reaction is not faster in a weaker acid.
  • B. Incorrect: the rate is slower, not faster.
  • C. Incorrect: the total volume is not halved because the same amount of magnesium reacts.
  • D. Correct: slower rate, same total hydrogen volume.

Exam key idea: Weak acids react more slowly than strong acids of similar concentration, but excess acid still gives the same total gas if the metal amount is unchanged.

chapter: Acids, Bases and Salts · Carbonates with acids
title: Which products are formed when magnesium carbonate reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid?
options: carbon dioxide, hydrogen and magnesium chloride
carbon dioxide and magnesium chloride only
carbon dioxide, water and magnesium chloride
answer: C. carbon dioxide, water and magnesium chloride
explanation:
Carbon dioxide, water and magnesium chloride are formed.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Carbonates react with acids to form a salt, water and carbon dioxide.
  2. Here the metal carbonate is magnesium carbonate, and the acid is hydrochloric acid.
  3. The salt formed is magnesium chloride.
  4. So the products are carbon dioxide, water and magnesium chloride.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Incorrect: hydrogen is not produced when a carbonate reacts with an acid.
  • B. Incorrect: water is missing.
  • C. Correct: acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide.
  • D. Incorrect: carbon dioxide is also formed.

Exam key idea: General reaction: acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide.

title: Dilute hydrochloric acid is titrated against aqueous sodium hydroxide.
context:
At the start of the titration, dilute hydrochloric acid is added to a conical flask using a .......1.......

A few drops of methyl orange indicator are added to the dilute hydrochloric acid in the conical flask.

Aqueous sodium hydroxide is added .......2....... until the colour of the indicator just .......3.......

Which row completes the gaps 1, 2 and 3?
options: burette; 1 cm<sup>3</sup> at a time; changes
volumetric pipette; 1 cm<sup>3</sup> at a time; disappears
explanation:
Use a volumetric pipette to transfer the acid, then add alkali dropwise until the indicator just changes colour.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. A titration starts with a measured volume of one solution in the conical flask. A volumetric pipette is used for this accurate transfer.
  2. The other solution is run from a burette into the flask. Near the end-point it must be added slowly, dropwise.
  3. Methyl orange does not disappear; it changes colour at the end-point.
  4. So the correct row is: volumetric pipette, dropwise, changes.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Correct: this gives the right apparatus and end-point technique.
  • B. Incorrect: titrations are not done by adding 1 cm³ at a time near the endpoint, and the colour does not disappear.
  • C. Incorrect: the acid is not added to the flask using a burette in this setup.
  • D. Incorrect: a burette is not used for the initial measured acid in the flask.

Exam key idea: In titration: pipette into flask, burette above, add dropwise until the indicator just changes colour.

title: Four aqueous substances are listed.
context:
1     ammonium carbonate

2     calcium sulfate

3     potassium chloride

4     sodium nitrate

Which two substances, when added together, will give a precipitate?
explanation:
Ammonium carbonate and calcium sulfate form a precipitate of calcium carbonate.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Look for a pair that can swap ions to make an insoluble salt.
  2. Ammonium carbonate provides CO₃²⁻ ions and calcium sulfate provides Ca²⁺ ions.
  3. Calcium carbonate is insoluble, so a precipitate forms. The other possible products remain soluble.
  4. Therefore substances 1 and 2 give a precipitate.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Correct: CaCO₃ precipitates when 1 and 2 are mixed.
  • B. Incorrect: ammonium and potassium salts remain soluble.
  • C. Incorrect: calcium nitrate and sodium sulfate are soluble.
  • D. Incorrect: potassium and sodium salts are usually soluble and no precipitate forms.

Exam key idea: A precipitate forms when two aqueous solutions produce an insoluble salt.

title: Which statements about the Periodic Table are correct?
context:
1     The horizontal rows of the Periodic Table are called groups.

2     The Periodic Table is arranged in order of increasing proton number.

3     The elements in the second column from the left of the Periodic Table form ions with a charge of 2+.

4     Elements in a horizontal row of the Periodic Table become more metallic going from left to right.
explanation:
Statements 2 and 3 are correct.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Horizontal rows are called periods, not groups, so statement 1 is false.
  2. The modern Periodic Table is arranged by increasing proton (atomic) number, so statement 2 is true.
  3. The second column from the left is Group 2; these metals form 2+ ions, so statement 3 is true.
  4. Metallic character decreases across a period from left to right, so statement 4 is false.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Incorrect: statement 1 is false.
  • B. Incorrect: both 1 and 4 are false.
  • C. Correct: statements 2 and 3 are true.
  • D. Incorrect: statement 4 is false.

Exam key idea: Rows are periods, columns are groups, and Group 2 elements form 2+ ions.

title: Which statement about alkali metals is correct?
options: Sodium is more reactive than potassium.
Sodium has a higher melting point than potassium.
Potassium has more outer-shell electrons than sodium.
answer: C. Sodium has a higher melting point than potassium.
explanation:
Sodium has a higher melting point than potassium.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. Down Group 1, melting points decrease, so sodium has a higher melting point than potassium.
  2. Lithium is less dense than sodium, so option A is wrong.
  3. Reactivity increases down the group, so potassium is more reactive than sodium.
  4. All Group 1 metals have one outer-shell electron, so potassium does not have more than sodium.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Incorrect: lithium is less dense than sodium.
  • B. Incorrect: potassium is more reactive than sodium.
  • C. Correct: melting point decreases down the group, so Na > K.
  • D. Incorrect: both have one outer-shell electron.

Exam key idea: In Group 1, reactivity increases down the group while melting point decreases.

title: Which row describes the difference in malleability between alloys and pure metals and explains the difference?
options: less malleable; different-sized atoms slide more easily over each other
less malleable; different-sized atoms slide less easily over each other
more malleable; different-sized atoms slide more easily over each other
more malleable; different-sized atoms slide less easily over each other
answer: B. less malleable; different-sized atoms slide less easily over each other
explanation:
Alloys are less malleable because different-sized atoms slide less easily over each other.

Step-by-step explanation

  1. In a pure metal, layers of atoms can slide over each other fairly easily.
  2. In an alloy, atoms of different sizes distort the regular arrangement.
  3. This makes the layers harder to slide, so the alloy is less malleable.
  4. Therefore the correct row is B.

Why each option is correct or incorrect

  • A. Incorrect: different-sized atoms do not slide more easily.
  • B. Correct: alloys are less malleable because the layers slide less easily.
  • C. Incorrect: alloys are usually less, not more, malleable than pure metals.
  • D. Incorrect: if sliding is less easy, the metal becomes less malleable, not more.

Exam key idea: Alloys are harder and less malleable because their layers are distorted by atoms of different sizes.
